llm.summary: RNG was entered on a watch list, achieved strong positive excess return but was stopped out on premature stop noise. The outcome was positive alpha with a process fault of over-sensitive stops truncating the move.
llm.root_cause: RNG was entered on a watch list, achieved strong positive excess return but was stopped out on premature stop noise. The outcome was positive alpha with a process fault of over-sensitive stops truncating the move.
llm.lesson: Watch-list entries with thin stops can be whipsawed by intraday noise; the stop engine needs to distinguish regulatory noise from structural reversal.
llm.engines_credit: The alpha engine correctly identified the opportunity; the stop-loss book lagged by firing on noise, not a confirmed trend break.
alternate_explanations: The stop may have been triggered by a company-specific event (e.g., earnings, guidance) not captured in the provided data.
The observed excess return could be partly due to market rotation into IT names, not just company-specific strength.
missing_evidence: intraday price and volume data around the stop trigger
stop-loss parameter settings and historical stop performance for this name
trailing stop logic and volatility adjustment

signal_hypotheses.feature: Ratio of stop-triggered exits that occur within 3 days of entry to total stops for watch-list names
signal_hypotheses.measurement: Compute over trailing 6 months of watch-list trades
signal_hypotheses.expected_direction: Higher ratio should correlate with larger post-trigger reversals (whipsaw losses)
signal_hypotheses.falsifier: If the ratio does not correlate with post-trigger excess returns, the hypothesis fails.
